analysis.title: Marketcolour + Cross-Asset / Consumer Outlook / Earnings (Ioannis Blekos, 10 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher on solid volumes: SPX +235bps to 7549, DJIA +215bps to 52389, NDX +274bps to 25253. All 11 sectors rose and 423 stocks were up. VIX fell 22.31% to 19.92. Tech rose 4.42%, Industrials 3.52%, Comm Services 2.49%.
NVDA fell 4.3% while SOX rose 6.85%, so the semiconductor rally was broader than NVDA.
Crude fell about 5% to $85 on further Iran de-escalation, which helped sentiment.

In Europe, AI names (EU Semis GSSBSEMI +4.82%) and Italian banks (GSXEITBK +4.65%) outperformed. The bank move followed Credit Agricole/BAMI M&A and strong UCG earnings. EU Cyclicals vs Defensives (GSPECYDE) rose 2.2%.
GS saw long-only buying in old favourites such as RR, LN, AIR FP, ASML NA and SAP GY.
US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of total US net market value. That is in the 1st, 1st and 3rd percentiles on 1-year, 3-year and 5-year lookbacks.

Retail bought last week's selloff. Leveraged ETFs took record inflows of +$3.3bn on Thursday. SOXL took +$5.1bn in 5-day net inflows, most of the buying in the leveraged category. TQQQ, SNXX, GDXU and NVDL also benefited.

Flow was a mix of covering and long buying across Tech (ex-NVDA, on weekend headlines). The market is hesitant to call an all-clear ahead of CPI (GIR forecast +16bps for core MoM) and CRWV/NBIS earnings later this week. GS floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale.
Asset manager flows were roughly flat, with demand in tech and financials and supply in comm services. Hedge funds were net buyers, largely through macro products.

GS cross-asset is overweight equities over 3m and 12m, citing earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end. It stays overweight cash because AI uncertainty and Middle East tensions may keep volatility elevated near term.

GS sees three paths to a rebound in risk appetite: easing AI concerns with signs of monetisation, rates relief helped by lower energy prices, and a larger decline of its RAI below -1, which improves the asymmetry for adding risk.

GS expects US consumer spending growth of 2.2% in 2027 (Q4/Q4), near potential. It expects a softer start as higher rates weigh on durables, energy prices stay elevated and nonprofit spending declines after the midterms. A pickup follows as inflation pressure fades and fiscal impulse turns modestly positive from tax refunds and reversed benefit cuts.

In US semis GS favors NVDA and AVGO, which it says imply no growth from 2027. In semi cap equipment it sees 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX. Memory is approaching oversold levels as it moves toward tangible book.

Rheinmetall is rated Buy, PT EUR2100, at 7x EBITDA. After a CEO fireside, GS says the company is confident the Arminius programme proceeds, artillery ammunition outlook is supportive, and there is a naval pipeline across new-build, maintenance and ship repair.

Infineon (IFX) Q4 was in line and Q4/FY27 guidance was in line. Data centre guidance of close to EUR4B is ahead of the sellside but below the buyside's >EUR4B hope. Q4 revenue was EUR4.71B in line, EBIT EUR1.12B vs consensus EUR1.10B, margin 23.8% vs consensus 23.3% and guidance of about 23%. GS calls the FX guide conservative.

Sunrise Q3 was in line with the Street and guidance was reiterated. Revenue was CHF732m. Adj FCF was CHF32.5M vs CHF36.7M a year ago, a miss on working capital. OFCF beat on lower capex. FY26 guidance was confirmed.
GS upgraded Pluxee to Neutral from Sell, PT EUR12.20, after share price underperformance and another reset of earnings expectations. It sees risk/reward as more balanced.
